title: How Does Your Phone Know Where You Are?
sources: GPS.gov, 'Space Segment': GPS satellites fly in medium Earth orbit at about 20,200 km and circle the Earth twice a day; the constellation has around 31 operational satellites (24-slot baseline)

GPS.gov / NASA 'What is GPS?': each satellite carries atomic clocks and continuously broadcasts its position and the time; receivers use the signal travel time (at the speed of light) to compute distance

GISGeography 'How GPS Receivers Work – Trilateration' / HowToGeek 'How GPS actually works': a receiver needs signals from at least four satellites to fix 3D position and correct its own clock (trilateration)

Penn State GEOG 862 'The Satellite Clock' / Ashby, 'Relativity in the Global Positioning System' (Living Reviews in Relativity 2003): satellite clocks gain about 38 microseconds per day relative to ground clocks (general minus special relativity); uncorrected, position errors would grow by roughly 10 km per day
GPS.gov / University of New Brunswick 'How does GPS work?': GPS is one-way; receivers are passive and do not transmit to the satellites

lines.text: How does your phone know exactly where you are?
lines.caps: HOW DOES YOUR *PHONE | KNOW *EXACTLY | WHERE YOU *ARE?

lines.text: around thirty GPS satellites circle the Earth,
and each one sends where it is and the exact time,
lines.caps: AND EACH *ONE | *SENDS | WHERE IT *IS | AND THE *EXACT | *TIME

lines.text: from an atomic clock on board.
Your phone catches a few and checks how late each signal arrived,
lines.caps: YOUR PHONE *CATCHES | A *FEW | AND *CHECKS | HOW *LATE | EACH *SIGNAL | *ARRIVED

lines.text: and since they fly at light speed, that delay gives the distance.
lines.caps: AND SINCE THEY *FLY | AT LIGHT *SPEED | THAT *DELAY | GIVES THE *DISTANCE

lines.text: With four of them, there's just one spot where the distances meet,
lines.caps: WITH *FOUR | OF *THEM | THERE'S JUST *ONE | *SPOT | WHERE THE *DISTANCES | *MEET

lines.text: Here's the twist: up there, clocks run a tiny bit fast, thanks to Einstein,
lines.caps: HERE'S THE *TWIST | UP *THERE | CLOCKS *RUN | A *TINY | BIT *FAST | THANKS TO *EINSTEIN

lines.text: and without a fix, your blue dot would drift ten kilometres a day!
lines.caps: AND WITHOUT A *FIX | YOUR BLUE *DOT | WOULD *DRIFT | TEN *KILOMETRES | A *DAY!

lines.text: And your phone never talks back. It just listens.
lines.caps: AND YOUR *PHONE | NEVER TALKS *BACK | IT JUST *LISTENS
